I played this a long while ago, but I never got around to reviewing it until now. 

The term “No other game quite like it” is bandied around a fair bit, but this game genuinely earns that term. SDD is one of the most refreshingly weird games I have ever played, and I really wish I could re-experience it for the first time again. 

Gameplay-wise, SDD is a very good RPG Metroidvania that has a fun cooldown-based combat system, which encourages you to weave together a lot of different abilities rather than just spamming one or two like in other similar games, and while the exploration can be slightly obtuse sometimes, it really rewards deductive reasoning and memorisation of the places you go. 

If the gameplay was all there was to go on, it would be good already, but where it really shines is the way it’s presented. I don’t want to spoil much more than what is shown in the trailer, but the visuals of the game are absolutely fantastic – There is an ongoing surrealist comedy vibe through the backgrounds and character design, and it makes the whole thing pretty unforgettable. 

The writing of the game is also very good, with a story that ended up being surprisingly gripping, especially towards the ending. There’s also a lot of comedy in the game, but this is where I need to point out a bit of a flaw: The sense of humour can be quite polarising. Depending on the sort of humour that you enjoy, the game will either be a continual riot, or the running gags will start to grate on you long before the end of the game. To specify, if you dislike the styles of humour where [spoiler]the vast majority of the cast are awful people towards the protagonist and they never get any comeuppance for it[/spoiler], [spoiler]a problem is caused or worsened because the protagonist is unable/unwilling to say anything[/spoiler], or [spoiler]the game forces you to do a bad thing and then repeatedly admonishes / comedy-guilt-trips you for it[/spoiler], the game might get on your nerves a bit. I did find these annoying, but the strength of the rest of the writing, visuals, and gameplay made up for it. 

Also, there is one legitimate complaint that I have with the game. Many Metroidvania games encourage you to explore everywhere once you’re fully kitted out, and SDD is no different, but there’s a pretty notable issue: Once you reach a certain point in the story, the music in the main hub area completely vanishes, and it makes a lot of the exploration feel very sterile. What’s worse is that the game locks you into an ending sequence, but gives you an opportunity to go back to before the endgame situation occurs, but this “point of no return reversal” puts you at a point after the music goes away. This might not be a dealbreaker to most, but it did dampen the experience a bit. If you are interested in the game and feel that this music-loss would be a problem for you, I strongly suggest you make a hard-save after defeating the boss at the end of the quest [spoiler]”Target: History”[/spoiler]. 

These are, however, small nitpicks in a game I absolutely adored. I played it a long while back, but after making this review, I intend on giving it another fresh playthrough. Highly recommended.

I picked this up during the last Steam sale for about 3 bucks and at that price I'd highly recommend it. Super Daryl Deluxe is an odd one. More of a beat em up than a Metroidvania or perhaps more accurately an RPGvania as the store page describes. It's a wacky adventure that truly shines when you're exploring this bizarre world that the devs created. The writing for this game is brilliant in that it never takes itself seriously and there were a lot of laugh out loud moments. A light spoiler, but one of the highlights for me is a section of the game where you rescue Ebenezer Scrooge from the ghost of Christmas past. This is turn prevents him from learning any lessons and instead vowing to spend the rest of his life eradicating ghosts and trust me there's an amazing payoff for this later in the game.

The game itself is a bit repetitive but fun. The combat reminded me of The World Ends With You. Daryl can equip 4 abilities, and later 8, to different buttons. Each one has different effects and cooldowns so you rotate through them quickly. There's a nice variety to them too. Unfortunately this is where my main criticism comes in. I find there's just too much of it. This game has a lot of side quests and they all boil down to killing a ton of enemies or collecting things they drop. It can become quite monotonous. There's one particular stretch through a massive pyramid dungeon that just never seemed to end. Also because there are no autosaves you can lose a bit of progress if you die before finding a save point. The other major problem for me is that this game does have some issues with crashing. My game crashed 4 times during my 20 hour playthrough, but the worst was right at the start it crashed when I was saving my game. This wiped my save file and since the game has no autosave, I had to start the game over. If this had happened later on I'd have dropped it completely. Unfortunately I don't think this game did well and I don't think we'll be seeing any patches to address these issues. I'd recommend saving to a different slot every time you do just in case, although it only happened that one time.

Aside from those issues I do recommend Super Daryl Deluxe. When you're engaging with the world and the characters it's a 10/10 for me. There's so many great jokes, great set ups with side quests and payoffs for the long running ones. The world itself is bizarrely fascinating. Whenever the gameplay got tiresome I pressed on to see what would happen next. I do hope that we may see a sequel or just another game from the team behind Daryl. It's a fun game that I'd love to see improved upon in a future entry. For 3.99 I can look past the flaws and I say you should definitely give it a try.

Don't by this crash happy game!

I played this game coop, and we experienced many crashes.  The worst one happened right at the freaking end of the final boss of the game.  Meaning we had to redo the entire, multi-phase fight!  And to further add salt to the wound, there's a lengthy, unskippable cutscenese that plays before the final phase.  Thankfully, that crash and MOST of the other crashes didn't happen again after we re-launched the game.  However, one crash kept happening and almost soft-locked our entire run.  We had to install the game on a different machine to get past that frustrating run.  Also, there's no auto-saving in this game.  Meaning, you have to save at save points.  Meaning if the game crashes and you haven't saved in a while, then guess what you have to do?

Aside from the crashing crap, another issue is that the combat in this game isn't good.  This is a game where enemies will keep spawning in the area, and they love to swarm and gang up on you.  And while there is invincibility frames when you get hit, its still very easy for you to lose most or all of your health very easily.  This is also one of those games where you can't aim your attacks, and flying enemies REALLY love to come at you in angles which make them difficult to hit.  Also, this is one of those games where if you aren't at the correct level and don't have the correct equipment, you will get killed very easily.  So, expect to grind.

The platforming is also a bit fiddly.  While platforming isn't a major part of the game, when it is needed, it's not all that fun.

As for the story, it is admittedly funny at times, but in like the last half or third, it gets VERY exposition and lore heavy.  And this is not one of those plots that should not be very lore heavy as its pretty stupid and cliché.  So, while I was fine with it at first, I was getting tired of it by the end.  Also, the ending is incredibly anti-climatic (which combined with the crashing issue we experienced made the whole thing crappy).

The game does at least nail the indie/high school/punky/Napoleon Dynamite style, but that is NOT enough to redeem all the crap we endured.  DO NOT BUY!

Listen - I would really like to love this game. The artstyle and art are incredible, and you can tell there was so much love and unique craziness poured into the visuals. As a very linear platform type game, this probably would've been fine, or even a point'n'click adventure - but that's not what it is. It's a very repetitive side-scrolling brawler in a very confusing environment with a map that's very hard to read, tons of locked doors that won't open until a random quest tells you it opens and countless fetch quests that ask you to kill the same enemies over and over and over and over and over again until you got 25 of whatever rare item they drop.

The humor, creative artstyle and zaniness in this game are undeniable, but it's ruined by said fetch quests, the overly wordy dialogue (which is admittedly pretty funny, but can't be easily skipped or sped through) and the combat as well as the technical issues. On Steam Deck, some people have reported crashes - I did not experience those, but the menu has glitched out for me several times, leaving me unable to cycle through the tabs I need to read quest info or look at a bigger map. You can hold the select button for a radial menu, which is a workaround, but this still shouldn't happen. The loading times are way too long as well, especially the minute it takes to load when the game starts up.

Combat is done by equipping  skills which all have their own internal cooldown. Often all those skills will be on cooldown, so you walk around until the cooldown resets - rinse and repeat. The skills themselves are creative and wacky, but there is no real flow to combat, no dodge button and no way to attack aside from skills, leading to a lot of standing or walking around while you can't do anything, while enemies are not subject to those restrictions.

The quests, as mentioned, aren't really that great. Most are fetch quests and an hour of playing was enough to realize what kind of gameplay was aimed for. Get quest, get 20 of a thing with rare droprates, turn in, rinse and repeat. Get quest to find a thing, have no idea where said thing is, not complete quest until you randomly stumble upon said thing in a completely different unconnected area. You need to do those quests to get stronger and unlock social skills which make you stronger too, so it's essentially just endless grinding with the mediocre combat until you're strong enough for the next story step. The map is confusing, many areas are inaccessible until the game allows you in, and you can explore pretty much any part of the school after the prologue, which leads to a lot of walking around aimlessly until you realize the area you're in has monsters way too strong for you and the map just isn't informative enough to quickly and easily point you in the right direction.

I wish this game was made to be a more linear sidescroller with better combat, or a point'n'click as mentioned - it would've been more fun and I would've been able to see more of the great artstyle and (mostly) good humor. In fact, I think the game would be incredible as some sort of zany adventure with puzzles. It's a shame it didn't click for me as the soundtrack isn't all that bad either. But playing the game, the main aspect of it, is repetitive, boring and one-dimensional - for a game that's reportedly 25-30 hours long, I can't imagine playing it for this long when it's issues become apparent so early. Amazing first impression, but sadly there is not much meat on the bones, and what's there went bad a while ago.

Fighting is repetitive.   There are times that all your moves are on cooldown and you can't even do anything.  You can swap out some moves for others but I don't enjoy this type of combat at all, I just feel like I'm spamming these buttons repeatedly.

It's almost like a beat 'em up, but I would much rather play any other one of those because at least my moves won't be on cooldown and there will be less silly dialogue.

Visuals were nice though.

I can't believe I didn't hear about this game until nearly 6 years after it was released. Super Daryl Deluxe is a ridiculous, goofy, surreal RPG adventure side-scroller. There were plenty of ridiculous moments that had me laughing throughout the ~30 hours I took to 100% complete the game. The combat is nice as you can assign any skill to any button. There's a decent enough challenge in combat and in exploration that doesn't demoralize you like Dark Souls but still keeps you on your toes. Just remember to save frequently, which you'll want to anyway since it fills your health. Some quest chains got a bit tedious with a lot of running back and forth, but no worse than things you'd see in other games. Honestly, the worst thing about the game is that there is kind of a small community - heck, there are no guides on Steam as of writing this.

Super Daryl Deluxe was definitely worth a shot. If you're on the fence, grab it during a Steam sale. It's sad this this game seemed to have gone unnoticed.

A 2D RPGvania(phrased by the devs and I like it) action adventure game that went completely unnoticed and lost in my backlog is borderline criminal. What I thought was going to be a pretty standard adventure turned into one of my all time favorites. 

The first rule of Super Daryl Deluxe, no spoilers

The game begins with a tutorial dream sequence as you take control of Daryl. You quickly learn how to swap powers in your locker and use them in combat while doing some simple platforming. This ends as Daryl is daydreamin during a story from the janitor of the school. The janitor continues with the prologue of the main backstory story which involves 2 geniuses from your school Eli and Kent who are responsible for world peace by writing a self help book but later are responsible for destroying it with another book called How to communicate with others. Funny, right? You then learn students and teachers at your new school are mysteriously missing and it's up to you to find out why. The game has a lot of comedic lines, tone and characters but around mid game it turns somewhat dark. And while Daryl does not talk nor ever change his emotions, which is very funny in a lot of situations, I really wish there was so much more voice acting(there is very, very little). It would have given more life to some really good characters that are everywhere in the game. I liked the story overall as it really kept me wanting to know more and the ending leaves some questions we probably will never receive and is kind of sad in all honesty. 

Super Daryl Deluxe(SDD) is an absolutely beautiful game that begins simply with the touches of bright orange on Daryl's pants and headband down to the white cowboy boots. These touches help you stick out in every scene whether it's simple conversing, exploring or combat.There are a ton of locations to explore all with different themes, styles and enemies. The game follows every 2D action game with some locations requiring X(a key in this case) to unlock certain paths. These keys are rare at the start but will become more accessible later in the game. The map you are equipped with is nice and easy to follow, but it will only show the region you are located. There is no full world map and no fast travel for a long time depending on how you play. This can have you running around on occasion of where you need to go next. I would caution those with sensitivity to bright flashing or abstract shaking as late in game this effect is everywhere and no options to lessen or disable. 

At the start you will be given a school ledger which is your inventory, map, info on friends and enemies, quests, and a diary that will update as you proceed in the game and will be a book by the time you are done. There is a ton of lore in the game, in fact there is a quest that will unlock a 20 page written diary that provides even more background info. The one missing element however is really about Daryl himself. There really is nothing that proclaims who he is or how he has these abilities, he is just the new kid in school looking for friends. 

This is a very no hand holding game with 47 main and 105 side quests with nothing showing on the map where to go. Majority of the time if you read back through the quest conversation in your diary you can figure it out…sometimes, but make no mistake you can get lost easily. The quests have lots of variety and I never was bored, however, a few late quests required constant backtracking and like the writing, a little cutting would not have hurt. 

As a 2D RPGvania Daryl excels in combat with a huge variety of enemies to defeat and large amounts of skills(46 total) to utilize. At the start you can equip 4 skills and a dodge mechanic but that will increase to 8 after completing a quest around half way. The skills all work on a cooldown, so butting mashing will not get it done. It's more of a rhythm dance of (using controller) RB(super), X(slash),B(range),LT(dash), Y(heal when needed) repeat as an example. Skills will be earned from completing main/ side quests and can also be purchased from the store. Each skill also comes with a grade from trash to excellent. The other thing is as you upgrade skills the animation for the power will change. As an example the ride the tide skill when activated at first shows you simply surfing over the enemy but once the power is maxed, you will be riding them over on a shark. These are very quick animations but knowing this happens for all 46 is amazing work from the dev team.

Combat in SDDis not too difficult, especially after you get some healing powers and there are no difficulty options, everything that flies in this game is a nuisance and there are a ton of them. But doing your button dance of powers and then enemies exploding into health and money balls is super satisfying. The hardest sections would be a few of the challenge rooms set up by your friends at the Dwarves and Druids club. Here you can choose battle training which requires(and equips) you with specific gear and powers but quests are for your current level and gear. These are both waved base challenges and you can earn Xp, PP, gear, weapons, etc. This can actually be exploited at the start to level but there is no reason. Also after beating certain bosses the same club will give you the option to defeat the boss again. It will be the same fight and each time will offer a piece of gear and collecting all of that boss's gear gives a nice bonus(if you wear them). Again, cool this option is here but with no change to the original fight it feels added for really no reason. 

Leveling is normal by completing quests, killing enemies, doing challenges, etc. There is a cap at 46 which I probably hit 2-3 hrs before the end. As you level you will instantly gain more health, defense, power and popularity points(PP). These PP points when reaching a level(15 total) will unlock a passive ability. The most important will be the double jump as it opens up so much more in terms of combat and exploration. 

As you level, explore and fight you will be given tons of loot to ponder(everything is instantly picked up btw) which includes the gear you will need to battle forward or items to complete quests. In your inventory you will be equipping 5 pieces of gear that includes the head, body, fists, and 2 trinkets that will offer bonuses to your stats. Some of these will come with passives and there are gear sets to offer even more bonus. I cannot recall a 2D game in which I was swapping gear and comparing stats so often. And while Daryl's look in game never changes, there is a hand drawn Daryl in the inventory that will show the gear you are equipping. Again, these little details highlight the attention the devs took for this title.

When quitting, you might need to backtrack a minute and a couple of maps; it's silly, yet much better than what I'd expect from the genre.

There are flaws, but all minor; they couldn't weigh in on my final appreciation:
- Texts appear character by character. The kind of stupid you'll find only in video games. Here, you must keep pressing the button for ages until things become fully readable. Next game will probably start writing the last characters, at the bottom right, then go backwards...
- Verbose. I like reading, but that much text excreted character by character, I had to skim.
- Some of the long conversations happen between save and boss fight. Sure, the boss fights are hard to lose, but the save should be after the not-worth-repeating talks anyway.
- Level cap. I hate those on a matter of principle. In practice though, I maxed out 10-15 hours too early and it didn't hurt the game at all.

There are three things a 'quirky' game has to do in order to be good. 
1, it can never be more annoying than it is funny. 
2 It can't just be quirky or weird or funny, it also has to be entertaining as gameplay. 
3 It has to be consisitent and interesting in its 'quirk' not stray outside of the central 'comedic' conceit. 
Thus I can conclude that Super Daryl Deluxe is an excellent 'quirky' game. 
Set in a high school after the worlds weirdest apocalypse you play Daryl, a gawky teen with the inability to refuse to do anythign anyone asks him to do. 
The world slowly strangens, and falls apart around you, and you just have to, keep doing quests, and hope that someone will eventually ask you to save the world. 
You get awesome powers, in an intersting combat system that forces you to build your own combos out of techniques that all have their own effedcts and cooldowns. 
Good game, 8/10. I played it for most of this week.

It is a somewhat entertaining yet weird game. The visual component is great, I really like that comic-book art and overall the style. The story is insane, but it's definitely not bad. Humor is actually pretty god to my liking. Some of the jokes really caught me off-guard. It's dark, but it's hilarious.

But than there are many things i do not like. 

First, Daryl himself. He's not good, he's not bad, he has no personality at all. I know that he's  a parody of those classic silent protagonist RPG heroes where you can thingk of the heroe's personality by yourself, but that does not work with Daryl. He has no personality period. Literally it is said so many times throghout the game that the protagonist is literal nobody with no real traits, no qualities and no preferences that eventually I could not stop addressing him as a piece of cardboard with useful skills to interact with outherwise pretty lively enviroment.

Second, the combat. While skills are interesting and there are many ways to use creative combo, the combat system feels clunky. I'd trade half of those skills for the remaning half being reliable.

Third, quests are often somewhat cryptic, and if you miss an important conversation point, you might get stuck without knowing what to do and where to go. I spent literal hours trying to pass the Haunted Mansion for the 1st time, even more in the Castle. Now I can understand the joy of discovery, but at some point a quest should give a clear hint how to progress with it.

Oh, and the last one: WHY IS EVERYBODY SO MEAN IN THIS GAME?
Literally, every single student seems to despise every other one. Even those who are supposed to be friends backstab, trick and frame each other. Even the possibly nicest guys you meet in the school, the DnD players, talk that they hate each other. And I won't even mention Honorary Students who mostly are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ by default. I know that this is a satire on high school where students fight for their future success, but it is just too dark in that sense. Why are there no relief no-matter-what good characters that you can rememebr fondly?

In fact, the only character that I could actually side for was that DnD girl who was turned into a Literature Guardian. She had a somewhat compelling and touching story. Too bad her story does not end well.

Overall, I would still recommend this game for sure. It's not great, but it is good, it is mostly fun, it is sometimes challenging and it is infuriating in a good way.

epic RPG

Думаю, одна из лучших игр, в которые я когда либо играл.

По сути - метроидвания с элентами рпг (прокачка персонажа, изучение новых способностей, фарм шмоток и денег, выполнение квестов от нпс).

На деле безумно оригинальная и необычная игра. Необычная в первую очередь атмосферой и сюжетом. Объективно - в играх такого плана сюжеты в целом повторяются. Или избранный герой спасает вселенную, или что-то мудреное и абстрактное про души/грехи/соль, из которых эта самая вселенная якобы состоит.

В этой же игре сюжет напоминает американские фильмы про школу из 70-80 годов. Главный герой - лузер и фрик, который переводится в новую школу и из неудачника постепенно превращается в супер героя, который спасает мир, встречает свою любовь ну и так далее. 

По аналогии с теми же фильмами 70-80х в игре огромное количество сюра и странных моментов. В школе открываются порталы в иные миры, в которых творится черт знает что. Примеры квестов в игре - помириться Наполена и Цезаря, помочь Бетховену победить ди-джея, пишущего модные римейки на его симфонические произведения, принести хоббиту кольцо всевластия, так как ему лень искать его самому.

Интересно, что при всем при этом в игре очень хороший и цепляющий сюжет, за которым реально интересно следить. Персонажи в игре отлично проработаны (а главные герои ещё и очень неплохо озвучены), диалоги написаны живо, много шуток, пародий и юмора, который не на сто, но процентов на 80 очень удачный. Игра очень длинная (часов 25 на просто прохождение без достижений и побочных квестов) и я лично за это время ни разу не заскучал, всегда интересно было узнать, как повернётся сюжет дальше, какие ещё странные и упоротые вещи будут происходить.

Насчёт технической стороны дела. Графика простая, но нарисовано со вкусом, все локации оформенны минималистично, но по-разному, каждая в своей стилистике, это разнообразие очень радует. Музыка - не фонтан, но и не раздражает, некоторые треки хороши.

Есть проблемы в части геймплея. В игре масса способностей, но они не очень сбалансированны, есть откровенно слабые, которые просто бесполезны. Есть довольно неприятные скачки в сложности, в целом игра простая, но на некоторых моментах можно дико застрять, особенно на паре боссов. В то же время драки очень красочные, у всех способностей своя анимация, которая меняется при их прокачке, а некоторые способности образуют мощнейший связки, от которых враги буквально разлетаются в стороны.

Итого - шикарная игра, необычная, интересная, сделанная очень качественно. То, что она прошла почти незамеченной - катастрофа.

Насколько мне удалось понять, за то недолгое время проведённое в игре, мы играем за молчаливого(но это не напрягает) школьника с невероятно бурной фантазией. В этой самой школе, будучи новичком, тебя знакомят со здешними обитателями, правилами и ролевой игрой называемой Dwarfs and Druids.
В итоге сходя с ума от безделия и непонимания почему почти все занятия отменены и в школе творятся странные вещи шкила начинает "сходить с ума" и развлекаться кто как может: кто-то подкалывает чуваков путём вредительства, кто-то эрпэшЫт, кто-то- просто хлебушек.
Тебя, как новенького, встречает множество квестов, прокачки и многого другого. Как я уже писАл, благодаря очень бурному воображению обычное "укради книгу" превращается в целые приключения с босс-файтами, атакующими колбами в кабинете химии и т.д..

[h1]Вывод[/h1]

Рисовка очень даже своеобразная, но приятная. По оптимизации полный порядок. Механики простые и понятные. Мини-карта, карта, подробный журнал, ветки прокачки и т.д.- присутствуют.
В общем, не знаю насчёт фуллпрайса, но за 108 деревянных настоятельно рекомендую ознакомиться!

I bought the game more than one year ago, and just recently had the time to finish it. I have to say that it has become one of my favorite games that I've ever played. It's a metroidvania full of comedy, action, references (to high culture, popular culture, videogames culture and even to the self game XD), good drama, and lots of epicity. I really would like to point specific things to explain it, but no one likes long reviews and, more importantly, I don't want to spoil anything (all I can say is that I felt the need to complete all the achievements and that's what I ended up doing). And, btw, loved the graphics and music (I would say it's like neo-retro).
Is it perfect? Being totally honest: no. As most games, it has some (very) tiny bugs (that if you aren't looking for, you would probably won't notice) and maybe the balance of the curve of power is not quite on point (this is even more understandable knowing how small the team was). However, do I recommend it? Oh, yeah.
